title: The Real Cost of a Six-Wheel Truck

scenes.text: A Mercedes G 63 AMG 6x6 cost about five hundred eleven thousand dollars new, and one sold at auction in twenty twenty for over nine hundred thousand. So what does a six-wheel truck really cost? The purchase price is only the start. In this video we work through fuel, tyres, mileage limits and resale, using published numbers, and we show where the sources go quiet.
scenes.caption: THE REAL COST OF A SIX-WHEEL TRUCK

scenes.text: Our sources are Autocar, Fox News, Wikipedia, Gear Patrol, The Drive, Motor Authority, Carscoops, MercedesBlog, Ford Authority, DuPont Registry, a tyre retailer, and the Energy Information Administration. Some figures are estimates, and some of our calculations rest on assumptions that we state. Our own arithmetic is labelled.
scenes.caption: SOURCES: AUTOCAR · FOX NEWS · WIKIPEDIA · GEAR PATROL · THE DRIVE · MOTOR AUTHORITY · CARSCOOPS · MERCEDESBLOG · FORD AUTHORITY · DUPONT REGISTRY · A TYRE RETAILER · EIA · ESTIMATES AND ASSUMPTIONS ARE LABELLED

scenes.text: Start with what it cost new. CarAdvice and Carscoops give three hundred seventy-nine thousand euros. Carscoops converts that to five hundred eleven thousand dollars in twenty thirteen. Autocar, in its February twenty fourteen review, gave three hundred seventy thousand pounds. By our arithmetic, the pound figure is about two point four percent below the euro one, before exchange rates.
scenes.caption: €379,000 (CARADVICE, CARSCOOPS) ≈ $511,000 IN 2013 (CARSCOOPS) · AUTOCAR (23 FEB 2014): £370,000 · £370,000 ÷ 379,000 = 97.6% — DIFFERENT CURRENCIES, NUMBERS ONLY (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Other outlets differ. Gear Patrol quoted about five hundred twenty-six thousand dollars in March twenty thirteen, and CarAdvice nearly five hundred fifty thousand. Autocar, as relayed by Fox News, said it would be priced second only to a battery-powered AMG sports car, which the Fox piece lists at five hundred fifty thousand dollars. We use the euro price and the Carscoops dollar figure.
scenes.caption: GEAR PATROL (MAR 2013): ~$526,000 · CARADVICE: 'NEARLY $550,000' · FOX NEWS (4 MAR 2013, CITING AUTOCAR): SECOND ONLY TO AMG E-CELL, LISTED AT $550,000 · WE USE €379,000 / $511,000

scenes.text: Autocar also says the price was more than three times that of the standard G 63 AMG. We do not have the G 63's price in our notes, so we cannot check that ratio. What we can say is that the 6x6 was not a trim level: it was a different product at a different order of price, and sold out as such.
scenes.caption: AUTOCAR: PRICE 'MORE THAN THREE TIMES THAT OF THE G 63 AMG' · G 63 PRICE: NOT IN OUR NOTES → RATIO NOT CHECKED

scenes.text: Now the Hennessey VelociRaptor 6x6. The Drive said two hundred ninety-five thousand dollars in October twenty sixteen, plus twenty-two thousand, five hundred for the HPE600 power package. Motor Authority said the twenty eighteen model started at three hundred forty-nine thousand, including the donor Raptor and the tune. An optional package added twenty-two thousand more.
scenes.caption: THE DRIVE (OCT 2016): $295,000 + $22,500 HPE600 · MOTOR AUTHORITY (OCT 2017): FROM $349,000 INCL. DONOR + TUNE; OPTIONAL PACKAGE +$22,000

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, the Mercedes cost about one hundred sixty-two thousand dollars, or forty-six percent, more than the Hennessey's start price. Fully optioned, the Hennessey would be three hundred seventy-one thousand, which narrows the gap to thirty-eight percent. These are launch prices four years apart, in different currencies. So treat the comparison as rough.
scenes.caption: $511,000 − $349,000 = $162,000 = +46.4% · $349,000 + $22,000 = $371,000 → +37.7% (OUR ARITHMETIC; 2013 vs 2017; EURO CONVERTED BY CARSCOOPS)

scenes.text: Fuel is the first running cost. Fox News, in March twenty thirteen, said fuel economy had not been determined for the 6x6, noting the 4x4 G 63 gets thirteen miles per gallon combined and suggesting the 6x6 would not be much better. Autocar later estimated around fifteen miles per gallon on the European test cycle.
scenes.caption: FOX NEWS (4 MAR 2013): 6x6 FUEL ECONOMY 'NOT DETERMINED'; 4x4 G63 = 13 MPG COMBINED, 6x6 'WON'T BE MUCH BETTER' · AUTOCAR (23 FEB 2014): ~15 MPG (EST), EUROPEAN TEST CYCLE

scenes.text: There is a catch. Autocar does not say whether that fifteen is in British or American gallons. A British gallon is larger. By our arithmetic, fifteen British miles per gallon would be about twelve and a half American. Wikipedia's G-Class page lists fifteen point six litres per hundred kilometres, which converts to fifteen American miles per gallon, but the cell is partly garbled.
scenes.caption: AUTOCAR: '15 MPG' — UNIT NOT STATED · 15 UK MPG ≈ 12.5 US MPG (OUR CONVERSION) · WIKIPEDIA G-CLASS PAGE: 15.6 L/100 KM = 15.1 US MPG (CELL PARTLY GARBLED)

scenes.text: We therefore model fuel with three assumptions: twelve and a half, thirteen and fifteen miles per gallon. For the price, the Energy Information Administration says regular gasoline averaged four dollars, twenty-eight cents a gallon in the week of the nineteenth of October twenty twenty-six. We do not know what fuel the 6x6 recommends, so premium would cost more.
scenes.caption: ASSUMED 12.5 / 13 / 15 MPG · EIA 19 OCT 2026: REGULAR $4.284/GAL · RECOMMENDED FUEL GRADE: NOT IN OUR SOURCES (PREMIUM WOULD COST MORE)

scenes.text: Fox News says the 6x6 has two twenty-one gallon tanks. Autocar says an overall capacity of one hundred fifty-nine litres, which matches. By our arithmetic, forty-two gallons at four dollars, twenty-eight cents is one hundred eighty dollars for a fill-up, and at thirteen miles per gallon that is about five hundred forty-six miles of range.
scenes.caption: FOX NEWS: TWO 21-GAL TANKS · AUTOCAR: 159 L OVERALL · 42 × $4.284 = $179.93 · 42 × 13 = 546 MI (OUR ARITHMETIC; REGULAR GRADE PRICE)

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, the cost per mile is about thirty-four cents at twelve and a half miles per gallon, thirty-three at thirteen, and twenty-nine at fifteen. These are fuel only. The numbers rest on the average regular price and on estimates of consumption, not a test of the truck.
scenes.caption: $4.284 ÷ 12.5 = $0.343/MI · ÷ 13 = $0.330/MI · ÷ 15 = $0.286/MI (OUR ARITHMETIC; ESTIMATED CONSUMPTION)

scenes.text: Then the year. Motor Authority says the United States Show or Display exemption allows up to twenty-five hundred miles a year. By our arithmetic, that costs about seven hundred fourteen to eight hundred fifty-seven dollars in fuel annually. A driver covering ten thousand miles, like the Japanese owner The Drive describes, would spend about twenty-eight fifty-six to thirty-four twenty-seven.
scenes.caption: 2,500 MI/YR: $714–$857 · 10,000 MI/YR: $2,856–$3,427 (OUR ARITHMETIC; $4.284/GAL; 12.5–15 MPG) · SHOW OR DISPLAY LIMIT: MOTOR AUTHORITY (R&T)

scenes.text: So fuel is not the main cost of this truck. By our arithmetic, even the highest fuel figure we calculated, thirty-four twenty-seven a year, is less than one percent of the five hundred eleven thousand dollar launch price. That is typical for very expensive vehicles driven little, though our sources do not compare it with other cars.
scenes.caption: $3,427 ÷ $511,000 = 0.67% (OUR ARITHMETIC) · COMPARISON WITH OTHER VEHICLES: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: Range is easy to check. Autocar says two tanks hold one hundred fifty-nine litres, and Fox News says two twenty-one gallon tanks. At the American thirteen miles per gallon, that is about five hundred forty-six miles. At twelve and a half it is five hundred twenty-five. Autocar's fifteen British miles per gallon on one hundred fifty-nine litres gives the same five hundred twenty-four, by our arithmetic.
scenes.caption: 159 L = 42 US GAL · 42 × 12.5 = 525 MI · 42 × 13 = 546 MI · 159 L = 35.0 UK GAL × 15 = 524 MI (OUR ARITHMETIC; ESTIMATED CONSUMPTION)

scenes.text: Per hundred miles, fuel costs about thirty-three dollars at thirteen miles per gallon, by our arithmetic. By that measure, the cost of one set of six tyres, forty-five twenty-seven, equals the fuel for about thirteen thousand, seven hundred miles. Again we use a proxy tyre and an assumed consumption, so this is a scale and not a forecast.
scenes.caption: $0.330 × 100 = $33 PER 100 MI · $4,527 ÷ $0.33 = 13,718 MI OF FUEL (OUR ARITHMETIC; PROXY TYRE; ASSUMED 13 MPG)

scenes.text: Tyres next. Wikipedia lists thirty-seven inch tyres on eighteen inch beadlock wheels, and Carscoops describes a Brabus car on Nitto Ridge Grappler tyres. A retailer lists the Nitto Ridge Grappler in thirty-eight by thirteen point five R eighteen at seven hundred fifty-four dollars forty-eight cents each. Its overall diameter is thirty-seven point seven inches.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: 37-IN TYRES, 18-IN BEADLOCK WHEELS · CARSCOOPS: NITTO RIDGE GRAPPLER · TYRE RETAILER: 38×13.50R18 = $754.48 EACH, OVERALL DIAMETER 37.7 IN (SIZE ASSUMED CLOSE ENOUGH — OUR ASSUMPTION)

scenes.text: We do not know that this is the exact tyre a 6x6 wears, so we use it as a proxy and flag it. By our arithmetic, six tyres at seven hundred fifty-four dollars forty-eight come to forty-five hundred twenty-seven dollars. With a matching spare, seven tyres would be fifty-two eighty-one. Mounting, balancing and shipping are not included.
scenes.caption: 6 × $754.48 = $4,527 · 7 × $754.48 = $5,281 (OUR ARITHMETIC; PROXY SIZE; EXCLUDES FITTING, SHIPPING, TAX)

scenes.text: Put the tyres in perspective. By our arithmetic, forty-five twenty-seven is about nine-tenths of one percent of the five hundred eleven thousand dollar launch price. The more important unknown is how long the tyres last. Our sources give no tyre life for the 6x6, and at low mileage age, not wear, may decide when they are replaced.
scenes.caption: $4,527 ÷ $511,000 = 0.89% (OUR ARITHMETIC) · TYRE LIFE FOR THE 6x6: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: The retailer shows a load rating of one hundred twenty-eight and a maximum single load of thirty-nine hundred seventy pounds per tyre. By our arithmetic, six tyres could carry up to twenty-three thousand eight hundred twenty pounds, well above the truck's weight of about nine thousand. This says the tyre is heavy duty, not what the truck's own rating is.
scenes.caption: RETAILER: LOAD INDEX 128, MAX 3,970 LB PER TYRE · 6 × 3,970 = 23,820 LB (OUR ARITHMETIC) vs TRUCK ~9,000 LB (WIKIPEDIA 9,001; THE DRIVE 9,050) · TRUCK'S OWN AXLE RATINGS: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: The Hennessey is different. Motor Authority says it comes with custom twenty-inch wheels and off-road tyres, but gives no size. So we cannot price its tyres at all from our sources. This is a case where the cheaper truck may not be cheaper to run, but we have no evidence either way and do not claim it.
scenes.caption: MOTOR AUTHORITY: CUSTOM 20-IN WHEELS, OFF-ROAD TYRES — SIZE NOT GIVEN → TYRE COST NOT COMPUTABLE · RUNNING-COST COMPARISON WITH MERCEDES: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: The Show or Display exemption shapes the whole cost picture in the United States. Motor Authority, citing a listing, says it allows limited road use up to twenty-five hundred miles per year. MercedesBlog adds that an NHTSA inspection is required until the car is twenty-five years old. The Drive says G and K Automotive Conversion made one road legal in Santa Ana.
scenes.caption: MOTOR AUTHORITY (R&T): SHOW OR DISPLAY, ~2,500 MI/YEAR · MERCEDESBLOG: NHTSA INSPECTION UNTIL 25 YEARS OLD · THE DRIVE: G&K AUTOMOTIVE CONVERSION, SANTA ANA, MADE A CAR ROAD LEGAL

scenes.text: No source gives what the import and conversion cost. That is a real part of the bill for any American buyer, and it is missing. So is the compliance work, registration, and the cost of inspections. We can only say that the legal route exists, and that the truck was never sold new in the United States according to our sources.
scenes.caption: IMPORT, CONVERSION, INSPECTION AND REGISTRATION COSTS: NOT IN OUR SOURCES · US NEW SALES: NONE REPORTED IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: The mileage limit has a nice effect on running costs. By our arithmetic, at twenty-five hundred miles a year, a car imported at five years old could cover at most twelve thousand, five hundred miles under that limit by age ten. The Brabus car in MercedesBlog covered eight thousand miles in eight years, a thousand a year, well under the allowance.
scenes.caption: 2,500 MI/YR × 5 = 12,500 MI (OUR ARITHMETIC) · MERCEDESBLOG: BRABUS CAR 8,000 MI IN 8 YEARS = 1,000 MI/YEAR (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: The Japanese car The Drive describes is the contrast: forty-eight thousand, nine hundred ninety miles, only about twenty-five hundred in America. The Drive estimates nearly nine thousand, five hundred miles a year under its earlier owner. Fuel and tyres for that use would be several times higher than the American numbers above, and our sources do not give its maintenance bills.
scenes.caption: THE DRIVE: 48,990 MI TOTAL, ~2,500 IN US · AUTHOR'S ESTIMATE ~9,500 MI/YEAR UNDER JAPANESE OWNER · MAINTENANCE BILLS: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: A word on weight, which drives wear on brakes and tyres. The sources disagree. Fox News said eight thousand three hundred pounds in March twenty thirteen. Autocar listed three thousand seven hundred seventy-five kilograms. Wikipedia lists four thousand eighty-three kilograms. The Drive says nine thousand fifty pounds for one car.
scenes.caption: FOX NEWS (2013): 8,300 LB · AUTOCAR (2014): 3,775 KG · WIKIPEDIA: 4,083 KG · THE DRIVE: 9,050 LB (ONE CAR)

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, Autocar's figure is about eight thousand three hundred twenty-two pounds, which matches Fox News. Wikipedia's is nine thousand and one pounds. The difference is eight percent. Early figures were probably from a prototype, but that is our guess, since Autocar's steering comment is about a prototype. The finished truck is the one in the nine thousand pound range.
scenes.caption: 3,775 KG = 8,322 LB · 4,083 KG = 9,001 LB → +8.2% (OUR ARITHMETIC) · AUTOCAR: 'VAGUE' STEERING ON THE PROTOTYPE · PROTOTYPE EXPLANATION = OUR GUESS

scenes.text: Now the number that overturns the usual logic: resale. The Drive reports a twenty fourteen G 63 AMG 6x6 sold for nine hundred one thousand, three hundred thirty-seven dollars on Bring a Trailer in November twenty twenty. By our arithmetic, that is three hundred ninety thousand, three hundred thirty-seven dollars more than the Carscoops launch equivalent of five hundred eleven thousand.
scenes.caption: THE DRIVE (10 NOV 2020): $901,337 · $901,337 − $511,000 = $390,337 (+76.4%) (OUR ARITHMETIC; 2013 EURO-TO-DOLLAR EQUIVALENT)

scenes.text: Over roughly seven years and eight months, from March twenty thirteen to November twenty twenty, that is an average gain of about seven point seven percent a year, by our arithmetic. This ignores import costs, taxes, dealer fees and the price actually paid by the first buyer in each market. It also compares a euro-based price with a dollar sale.
scenes.caption: (901,337 ÷ 511,000)^(1/7.7) − 1 ≈ 7.7%/YEAR (OUR ARITHMETIC; MAR 2013 → NOV 2020; EXCLUDES IMPORT COSTS, TAXES, FEES)

scenes.text: The Brabus-tuned car shows the other side. MercedesBlog says it sold in May twenty twenty-two for one million, one hundred seventy thousand, which was one hundred eighty thousand less than its previous price of one million, three hundred fifty thousand. By our arithmetic, that is a thirteen percent drop in about five months for the dealer who held it.
scenes.caption: MERCEDESBLOG (18 MAY 2022): $1,170,000 vs PREVIOUS $1,350,000 → −$180,000 = −13.3% · PREVIOUS SALE DEC 2021 → ~5 MONTHS (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Carscoops adds that in December twenty twenty-one this car had eight thousand miles and was set to sell for at least one point one million. It says you would not find a G 63 AMG 6x6 for less than a million dollars. MercedesBlog shows it sold below the earlier price. A resale market for a hundred cars is thin, and one sale moves it.
scenes.caption: CARSCOOPS (21 DEC 2021): 8,000 MI, 'AT LEAST $1.1 MILLION'; 'YOU WON'T FIND ONE FOR LESS THAN $1 MILLION' · ~100 CARS BUILT → FEW SALES (WIKIPEDIA, OTHERS)

scenes.text: Motor Authority's November twenty twenty piece lists used examples from nine hundred seventy-five thousand to one point six million. A bid then was five hundred sixty-seven thousand. The writer says it was not far above the original sticker. By our arithmetic, a bid at that level is eleven percent above five hundred eleven thousand, and the final sale reached nine hundred one thousand.
scenes.caption: MOTOR AUTHORITY (3 NOV 2020): BID $567,000 AT PUBLICATION; LISTINGS $975,000–$1.6 M · THE DRIVE (10 NOV 2020): FINAL $901,337 · $901,337 ÷ $567,000 = 1.59× (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: The Hennessey is more modest. Ford Authority reports a twenty eighteen model at its buy-now price of three hundred seventy-five thousand dollars on eBay, though it is not sure of the exact amount, and a twenty seventeen truck with six thousand miles at three hundred fifty-five thousand. By our arithmetic, that is seven percent above the three hundred forty-nine thousand start for the first.
scenes.caption: FORD AUTHORITY (FEB 2019): 2018 MODEL 'BUY NOW' $375,000 (EXACT SALE UNCERTAIN) · 2017 TRUCK, 6,000 MI, LISTED $355,000 · $375,000 ÷ $349,000 = +7.4% (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Try the per-mile view, which exposes the real price of low mileage. By our arithmetic, if an owner kept the Mercedes for ten years at twenty-five hundred miles a year, that is twenty-five thousand miles. Dividing the five hundred eleven thousand dollar launch price by that gives about twenty dollars and forty cents a mile, before any resale and before fuel or tyres.
scenes.caption: $511,000 ÷ 25,000 MI = $20.44/MI (OUR ARITHMETIC; 10 YEARS × 2,500 MI; BEFORE RESALE, FUEL, TYRES)

scenes.text: Resale changes that, if the market holds. By our arithmetic, buying at five hundred eleven and selling at nine hundred one thousand would leave a gain of three hundred ninety thousand, so the net cost of the truck over the period would be negative, before running costs. That depends on a single sale, taxes, and import costs we do not know.
scenes.caption: $901,337 − $511,000 = +$390,337 GAIN → NEGATIVE NET PURCHASE COST (OUR ARITHMETIC; ONE SALE; TAXES AND IMPORT COSTS UNKNOWN)

scenes.text: Now the buyer of the nine hundred one thousand dollar car. By our arithmetic, spread over the same twenty-five thousand miles, that is thirty-six dollars and five cents a mile before resale. Whether that car holds its value is an open question. Our sources show the Brabus car falling thirteen percent in five months in twenty twenty-one and twenty twenty-two.
scenes.caption: $901,337 ÷ 25,000 = $36.05/MI (OUR ARITHMETIC; BEFORE RESALE) · BRABUS CAR: −13.3% IN ~5 MONTHS (MERCEDESBLOG)
scenes.orig_query: Cost per mile for a later buyer

scenes.text: Price per pound is an odd but accurate measure. At the nine thousand and one pounds Wikipedia lists, the five hundred eleven thousand dollar price works out at about fifty-seven dollars a pound, by our arithmetic. At the Hennessey's three hundred forty-nine thousand dollars we cannot do the same sum, because no source gives its weight.
scenes.caption: $511,000 ÷ 9,001 LB = $56.77/LB (OUR ARITHMETIC; WIKIPEDIA WEIGHT) · HENNESSEY WEIGHT: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: Autocar's February twenty fourteen review adds some context to the cost. It said the 6x6 was remarkably easy to drive and that it felt invincible in the dunes, but called the steering vague on the prototype. It also noted the tyre compressor takes about twenty seconds to inflate from half a bar to one point eight bar, although the gallery text says two bar.
scenes.caption: AUTOCAR: 'REMARKABLY EASY TO DRIVE' · 'FEELS INVINCIBLE' IN THE DUNES · STEERING 'VAGUE' ON THE PROTOTYPE · COMPRESSOR ~20 S FROM 0.5 BAR TO 1.8 BAR (GALLERY TEXT SAYS 2.0)

scenes.text: Autocar also estimated zero to sixty-two miles per hour in six seconds, and said insiders suggested less than that, with a top speed electronically governed to one hundred miles per hour. Wikipedia lists seven point eight seconds to sixty. By our arithmetic, that is a gap of one point eight seconds, a measure of how uncertain the early figures were.
scenes.caption: AUTOCAR (2014): 0–62 MPH 6.0 S (EST), 'LESS THAN SIX' PER INSIDERS · WIKIPEDIA: 0–60 7.8 S · 7.8 − 6.0 = 1.8 S (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Why does that matter for cost? Because speed claims and weight claims were repeated for years, and buyers paid the prices on the strength of them. The sources we have show that the first numbers and the later ones differ by almost ten percent on weight. A careful buyer would want a measured figure, and none is in our notes.
scenes.caption: WEIGHT: 8,322 LB (AUTOCAR) vs 9,001 LB (WIKIPEDIA) = 8.2% · 0–60: 6.0 vs 7.8 S · MEASURED FIGURES FROM A TEST: NOT IN OUR NOTES

scenes.text: There is one more Mercedes price in the sources. Wikipedia says fifteen right-hand-drive units in Malaysia were bought by Naza World at three point two million ringgit before tax. By our arithmetic, fifteen units at that price would be forty-eight million ringgit. The article behind that figure concerns a Brabus car, so we flag it, and we do not convert it to dollars.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: MALAYSIA — 15 UNITS, NAZA WORLD, RM3.2 MILLION BEFORE TAX · 15 × 3.2 = RM48 MILLION (OUR ARITHMETIC) · CITED ARTICLE CONCERNS A BRABUS CAR — CAUTION · NOT CONVERTED

scenes.text: The costs we could not find matter most. Insurance. Servicing at a Mercedes dealer for an army-derived six-axle drivetrain. Storage for a truck almost twenty feet long. Transport. Parts for portal axles. We looked, and found no owner-published bills or independent estimates for any of them in the sources we can cite.
scenes.caption: NOT IN OUR SOURCES: INSURANCE · SERVICE COSTS · STORAGE · TRANSPORT · PARTS PRICES · OWNER-PUBLISHED BILLS · INDEPENDENT ESTIMATES

scenes.text: Length is one reason. Wikipedia lists the Mercedes at fifty-eight seventy-five millimetres, which by our arithmetic is nineteen point three feet, and about two metres ten wide. Tight garages and ordinary parking spaces may not suit that, but our sources do not discuss parking costs, so we leave it there.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: 5,875 MM LONG = 19.3 FT · 2,110 MM WIDE = 6.9 FT (OUR CONVERSION) · PARKING / STORAGE COSTS: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: Autocar's tester, Greg Kable, wrote that the truck is a fun thing to drive in the right conditions but a super-exclusive proposition for all but the mega-rich. He also called it remarkably easy to drive. That is his opinion in a February twenty fourteen review. It does not give a running cost, but it reflects who the price was for.
scenes.caption: AUTOCAR (GREG KABLE, 23 FEB 2014): 'A FUN THING TO DRIVE IN THE RIGHT CONDITIONS' · 'SUPER-EXCLUSIVE PROPOSITION FOR ALL BUT THE MEGA-RICH' · 'REMARKABLY EASY TO DRIVE' (OPINION)

scenes.text: Production was small. Fox News, citing Autocar, said Mercedes expected to build twenty to thirty units a year. Wikipedia says around one hundred were built over two years, and that more were sold than anticipated. By our arithmetic, that is about fifty a year, roughly two times the expected rate. A planned small run became a larger one.
scenes.caption: FOX NEWS (CITING AUTOCAR, 2013): 20–30 UNITS/YEAR EXPECTED · WIKIPEDIA: ~100 OVER 2013–2015 → ~50/YEAR = 1.7–2.5× EXPECTED (OUR ARITHMETIC) · WIKIPEDIA: 'MORE THAN ORIGINALLY ANTICIPATED'

scenes.text: Let us build a simple sheet from what we have, for an American owner at twenty-five hundred miles a year. Purchase, five hundred eleven thousand at launch. Fuel, seven hundred fourteen to eight hundred fifty-seven a year. One set of tyres, about forty-five hundred. Everything else, insurance and service, unknown. By our arithmetic that is the cheap part.
scenes.caption: PURCHASE $511,000 (2013 EQUIVALENT) · FUEL $714–$857/YEAR · TYRES ~$4,527 PER SET (PROXY) · INSURANCE, SERVICE, IMPORT, STORAGE: UNKNOWN (OUR SUMMARY)

scenes.text: Over five years, by our arithmetic, fuel is three thousand, five hundred seventy to forty-two eighty-five. Add one tyre set at forty-five twenty-seven and the known running cost is roughly eight thousand to nine thousand dollars. Against a resale gain of three hundred ninety thousand that the Drive's sale implies, these are small, but the unknowns could be larger.
scenes.caption: FUEL 5 × $714–$857 = $3,570–$4,285 · + TYRES $4,527 = $8,097–$8,812 (OUR ARITHMETIC; KNOWN ITEMS ONLY) · RESALE GAIN IMPLIED: $390,337 (ONE SALE)

scenes.text: A buyer today faces a different calculation. The entry ticket is now nine hundred thousand dollars and up, based on the used sales in our sources, and that is before import. By our arithmetic, nine hundred one thousand is one hundred seventy-six percent of the old five hundred eleven. Whether it keeps rising is unknown, since our sources record only past sales.
scenes.caption: RECENT USED REFERENCES: $901,337 (2020), $1,170,000 (2022 BRABUS) · $901,337 ÷ $511,000 = 176% (OUR ARITHMETIC) · FUTURE PRICES: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: The Hennessey sheet is shorter. Purchase, three hundred forty-nine thousand, plus optional twenty-two thousand. Fuel, unknown. Tyres, unknown. Weight, unknown. The only other number we found is the used price, around three hundred fifty-five to three hundred seventy-five thousand in early twenty nineteen. So for the cheaper truck, we know even less about the true cost.
scenes.caption: HENNESSEY: PURCHASE $349,000 (+$22,000 OPTION) · FUEL / TYRES / WEIGHT / INSURANCE / SERVICE: NOT IN OUR SOURCES · USED: $355,000–$375,000 (FORD AUTHORITY, FEB 2019)

scenes.text: What is missing. Any measured fuel economy for either truck. Insurance and service bills. The cost of importing and certifying a car in the United States. Tyre life. A depreciation curve rather than a few sales. If you have owned one of these, share a real number in the comments, and we will update the description.
scenes.caption: NOT IN OUR SOURCES: MEASURED FUEL ECONOMY · INSURANCE · SERVICE BILLS · IMPORT AND CERTIFICATION COSTS · TYRE LIFE · DEPRECIATION CURVE
scenes.chapter: What our sources do not say

scenes.text: So what does a six-wheel truck really cost? The sticker was five hundred eleven thousand dollars for the Mercedes and three hundred forty-nine thousand for the Hennessey. Running costs that we can compute are small beside that. And the used market, at least for the Mercedes, has so far paid more than new. Subscribe to Pickup Reality, and the twenty twenty-seven Truck Buyer's Guide is linked in the description.
scenes.caption: SUBSCRIBE: PICKUP REALITY
